method: Sequential exact-response replay of all 25 archived decisions to reconstruct wire inputs; final-frame four-condition ablation with rotating order, five repeats each; then five repeats of the actual earlier step-20 frontier request with identical pixels. Live Jev only, no browser actions or public-site requests. No expected answers or DOM labels supplied.
interpretation: Action selection repeatedly proposes an already executed scroll; frontier selection can select a previously image-judged promising entry, but stops on this final candidate set. The replay does not establish that stopping missed an accessible answer. Removing coverage did not reverse stopping; removing route judgments once selected a prohibited Download lead. No production bypass or forced-continuation fix is justified by these observations.
limits: Repeated calls over one archived Goal are not independent-site accuracy samples.
The earlier positive control changes history, target set and route judgments together. It proves context-sensitive route selection, not an isolated causal effect of one promising label.
Source-image equality and past scroll destinations prove a repeated view transition, not that every detail was understood or that revisiting is always useless.
No claim that password recovery information is absent from the entire site, that off-origin pages contain it, or that human UX failure is established.
No source-site revisit or production re-exploration occurred in this diagnostic.
Prior individual post-run evidence-selection inconsistency remains outside this stopping diagnosis.
